questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At 30°C the solubility of PbI_2$ salt in 0.2 M KI solution will be X, if the solubility product of PbI_2$ at 30°C is $2.4 \times 10^{-8}$. Identify the value of X.
questions.solution:
The dissociation of $PbI_2$ is given by:

$PbI_2(s) \rightleftharpoons Pb^{2+}(aq) + 2I^-(aq)$

Let the solubility of $PbI_2$ in $0.2$ M $KI$ solution be $s$.

The concentration of $I^-$ ions from $KI$ is $0.2$ M. Since $KI$ is a strong electrolyte, it completely dissociates. The total concentration of $I^-$ ions is $(2s + 0.2)$ M. Because $K_{sp}$ is very small, $2s$ can be neglected compared to $0.2$.

$[I^-] \approx 0.2$ M

The expression for the solubility product is:

$K_{sp} = [Pb^{2+}][I^-]^2$

Substituting the given values:

$2.4 \times 10^{-8} = s \times (0.2)^2$

$2.4 \times 10^{-8} = s \times 0.04$

$s = \dfrac{2.4 \times 10^{-8}}{0.04} = 6.0 \times 10^{-7}$ M

Thus, the solubility $X$ is $6.0 \times 10^{-7}$ M.

Answer: $6.0 \times 10^{-7}$M

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A buffer solution was prepared by mixing 5 g of acetic acid with 7.5 g of sodium acetate. The solution was made upto 500 mL . The pH of the resulting solution is:
$\left[p K_a=4.76\right]$
questions.solution:
The molar mass of acetic acid ($CH_{3}COOH$) is $60\text{ g/mol}$. The number of moles of acetic acid is $n_{acid} = \dfrac{5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{12}\text{ mol}$.

The molar mass of sodium acetate ($CH_{3}COONa$) is $82\text{ g/mol}$. The number of moles of sodium acetate is $n_{salt} = \dfrac{7.5}{82} \approx 0.09146\text{ mol}$.

Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer: $pH = pK_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[salt]}{[acid]} \right)$.

Since the volume is the same for both components in the $500\text{ mL}$ solution, the ratio of concentrations is equal to the ratio of moles: $pH = pK_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{n_{salt}}{n_{acid}} \right)$.

$pH = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{7.5/82}{5/60} \right) = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{7.5}{82} \times \dfrac{60}{5} \right) = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{1.5 \times 60}{82} \right) = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{90}{82} \right)$.

$pH = 4.76 + \log(1.0976) \approx 4.76 + 0.04 = 4.8$.

Answer: 4.8

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ionisation constant of the weak acid HF whose concentration is $0.1\text{ M}$ is $3.5 \times 10^{-4}$. The Equilibrium constant value for the reaction $\text{F}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HF} + \text{OH}^-$ is _____ and the pH of aqueous solution of the weak acid is _____.
questions.solution:
The reaction $F^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons HF + OH^-$ is hydrolysis of the conjugate base, so $K_{eq} = K_b = \dfrac{K_w}{K_a}$:

$K_{eq} = \dfrac{1.0 \times 10^{-14}}{3.5 \times 10^{-4}} \approx 2.86 \times 10^{-11}$

For pH, using $[H^+] \approx \sqrt{K_a \cdot C}$:

$[H^+] = \sqrt{3.5 \times 10^{-4} \times 0.1} = \sqrt{3.5 \times 10^{-5}} \approx 5.92 \times 10^{-3}$ M

$pH = -\log(5.92 \times 10^{-3}) \approx 2.23$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What volume of $0.2 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ needs to be added to $100 \mathrm{ml}$ of $0.4 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COONa}^2$ solution to prepare a buffer of pH equal to 4.91 ? ($\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ is 4.76)
questions.solution:
The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer is given by:

$\text{pH} = \text{pK}_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)$

Given $\text{pH} = 4.91$, $\text{pK}_{a} = 4.76$, and the concentration of salt $[\text{CH}_{3}\text{COONa}] = 0.4 \text{ M}$ with volume $V_{s} = 100 \text{ ml}$.

Substituting the values into the equation:

$4.91 = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{n_{\text{salt}}}{n_{\text{acid}}} \right)$

$0.15 = \log \left( \dfrac{0.4 \times 100}{0.2 \times V_{a}} \right)$

Taking the antilog of both sides:

$10^{0.15} = \dfrac{40}{0.2 \times V_{a}}$

$1.4125 = \dfrac{40}{0.2 \times V_{a}}$

$0.2 \times V_{a} = \dfrac{40}{1.4125}$

$0.2 \times V_{a} = 28.3186$

$V_{a} = \dfrac{28.3186}{0.2} = 141.59 \text{ ml}$

Answer: 141.59 ml

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Solubility product of the sparingly soluble salt $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ in aqueous medium is $9.3 \times 10^{-10}$ Calculate the mass in gram of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ present in 100 ml of its saturated solution.
(Molar mass of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ is $236 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ )
questions.solution:
The solubility equilibrium for $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ is given by:
$\mathrm{AgBrO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Ag}^{+}(aq) + \mathrm{BrO}_3^{-}(aq)$

Let $s$ be the solubility of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ in mol/L. Then $[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}] = s$ and $[\mathrm{BrO}_3^{-}] = s$.

The solubility product constant $K_{sp}$ is defined as:
$K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Ag}^{+}][\mathrm{BrO}_3^{-}] = s^2$

Given $K_{sp} = 9.3 \times 10^{-10}$, we have:
$s = \sqrt{9.3 \times 10^{-10}} = \sqrt{93 \times 10^{-11}} = \sqrt{9.3} \times 10^{-5} \approx 3.04959 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol/L}$

The volume of the solution is $100 \text{ ml} = 0.1 \text{ L}$.

The number of moles of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ in $0.1 \text{ L}$ is:
$n = s \times V = 3.04959 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol/L} \times 0.1 \text{ L} = 3.04959 \times 10^{-6} \text{ mol}$

The molar mass of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ is $236 \text{ g/mol}$. The mass $m$ is:
$m = n \times \text{Molar Mass} = 3.04959 \times 10^{-6} \text{ mol} \times 236 \text{ g/mol}$
$m = 719.705 \times 10^{-6} \text{ g} = 7.19705 \times 10^{-4} \text{ g}$

Answer: $7.197 \times 10^{-4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH at which an acid indicator with $K_\alpha=1 \times 10^{-5}$ changes colour when the indicator concentration is $1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ is
questions.solution:
An acid indicator is a weak acid. It dissociates
$\underset{\text { Colour } A}{\operatorname{HIn}} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}^{+}+\underset{\text { Colour } B}{\operatorname{In}^{-}}$
$K_{\mathrm{In}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]\left[\mathrm{In}^{-}\right]}{[\mathrm{HIn}]}$
The indicator HIn will show a colour change at mid point, i.e. the point at which $\left[\mathrm{In}^{-}\right]=[\mathrm{HIn}]$
Hence, $K_{\mathrm{in}}=\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=10^{-5}$
or $\quad \mathrm{pH}=5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $1 \mathrm{~cm}^3 \text { of } 0.01 \mathrm{~M} \mathrm{~HCl} \text { is added to } 1 \mathrm{~L} \text { of } \mathrm{NaCl} \text { solution. The } \mathrm{pH} \text { of the resulting solution is: }$
questions.solution:
The volume of the HCl solution added is $V_1 = 1 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L}$.

The concentration of the HCl solution is $M_1 = 0.01 \text{ M} = 10^{-2} \text{ M}$.

The total volume of the resulting solution is $V_2 = 1 \text{ L} + 0.001 \text{ L} \approx 1 \text{ L}$.

The number of moles of $\text{H}^{+}$ ions added is $n = M_1 \times V_1 = 10^{-2} \text{ mol/L} \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} = 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

The concentration of $\text{H}^{+}$ ions in the final solution is $[\text{H}^{+}] = \dfrac{n}{V_2} = \dfrac{10^{-5} \text{ mol}}{1 \text{ L}} = 10^{-5} \text{ M}$.

The pH of the solution is given by $\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^{+}] = -\log(10^{-5}) = 5$.

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What volume of $0.2 \mathrm{~M}$ Acetic acid is to be added to $100 \mathrm{ml}$ of $0.4 \mathrm{M}$ Sodium acetate so that a Buffer solution of $\mathrm{pH}$ equal to 4.94 is obtained? $(\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}=4.76)$
questions.solution:
The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer is given by:

$\text{pH} = \text{pK}_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)$

Given $\text{pH} = 4.94$, $\text{pK}_{a} = 4.76$, and the volume of salt ($V_{s}$) = $100 \text{ ml}$ with concentration ($M_{s}$) = $0.4 \text{ M}$. Let the volume of acid be $V_{a}$ with concentration ($M_{a}$) = $0.2 \text{ M}$.

Substituting the values into the equation:

$4.94 = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{M_{s} V_{s} / (V_{s} + V_{a})}{M_{a} V_{a} / (V_{s} + V_{a})} \right)$

$4.94 - 4.76 = \log \left( \dfrac{0.4 \times 100}{0.2 \times V_{a}} \right)$

$0.18 = \log \left( \dfrac{40}{0.2 V_{a}} \right)$

Taking the antilog of both sides ($10^{0.18} \approx 1.5136$):

$1.5136 = \dfrac{40}{0.2 V_{a}}$

$0.2 V_{a} = \dfrac{40}{1.5136}$

$0.2 V_{a} \approx 26.427$

$V_{a} = \dfrac{26.427}{0.2} = 132.135 \text{ ml}$

Answer: 132.1 ml

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $300 \mathrm{ml}$ of an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ with $\mathrm{pH}$ value of 10 is mixed with $200 \mathrm{ml}$ of an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{HCl}$ with a $\mathrm{pH}$ value of 4. What will be the $\mathrm{pH}$ of the resultant solution at room temperature?
questions.solution:
For the NaOH solution, $\text{pH} = 10$, so $\text{pOH} = 14 - 10 = 4$.

$[\text{OH}^{-}] = 10^{-4} \text{ M}$.

Moles of $\text{OH}^{-} = 300 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol/L} = 3 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

For the HCl solution, $\text{pH} = 4$, so $[\text{H}^{+}] = 10^{-4} \text{ M}$.

Moles of $\text{H}^{+} = 200 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol/L} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

Since $\text{OH}^{-}$ reacts with $\text{H}^{+}$ to form water, the remaining moles of $\text{OH}^{-}$ are $3 \times 10^{-5} - 2 \times 10^{-5} = 1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

Total volume of the mixture $= 300 \text{ ml} + 200 \text{ ml} = 500 \text{ ml} = 0.5 \text{ L}$.

Resultant concentration of $\text{OH}^{-} = \dfrac{1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}}{0.5 \text{ L}} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$.

$\text{pOH} = -\log(2 \times 10^{-5}) = 5 - \log 2 = 5 - 0.301 = 4.699$.

$\text{pH} = 14 - 4.699 = 9.301$.

Answer: 9.301

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{~B}_4$ is a sparingly soluble salt with a solubility of $\mathrm{s} g / \mathrm{L}$. If the Molar mass of $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{~B}_4$ is $\mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{mol}$, what is the expression for its $\mathrm{K}_{\text {sp }}$ ?
questions.solution:
The salt $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{B}_4$ dissociates in water as follows:

$\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{B}_4 (s) \rightleftharpoons 3 \mathrm{A}^{4+} (aq) + 4 \mathrm{B}^{3-} (aq)$

The solubility of the salt is given as $s$ g/L. The molar mass of the salt is $M$ g/mol. Therefore, the molar solubility $S$ in mol/L is given by:

$S = \dfrac{s}{M}$ mol/L

From the stoichiometry of the dissociation, the concentration of $\mathrm{A}^{4+}$ is $3S$ and the concentration of $\mathrm{B}^{3-}$ is $4S$.

The solubility product constant $K_{sp}$ is defined as:

$K_{sp} = [\mathrm{A}^{4+}]^3 [\mathrm{B}^{3-}]^4$

Substituting the concentrations in terms of $S$:

$K_{sp} = (3S)^3 (4S)^4$

$K_{sp} = (27 S^3) (256 S^4)$

$K_{sp} = 27 \times 256 \times S^7$

$K_{sp} = 6912 S^7$

Substituting $S = \dfrac{s}{M}$:

$K_{sp} = 6912 \left( \dfrac{s}{M} \right)^7$

Answer: $6912(\mathrm{~s} / \mathrm{M})^7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What would be the volume of water required to dissolve $0.2 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{PbCl}_2$ of molar mass $278 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ to prepare a saturated solution of the salt? $(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{SP}}$ of $\mathrm{PbCl}_2=3.2 \times 10^{-8})$
questions.solution:
The solubility equilibrium for $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ is given by $\text{PbCl}_{2}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Pb}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{Cl}^{-}(aq)$.

Let $s$ be the solubility of $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ in mol/L. Then $[\text{Pb}^{2+}] = s$ and $[\text{Cl}^{-}] = 2s$.

The solubility product constant is $K_{sp} = [\text{Pb}^{2+}][\text{Cl}^{-}]^{2} = s(2s)^{2} = 4s^{3}$.

Given $K_{sp} = 3.2 \times 10^{-8}$, we have $4s^{3} = 3.2 \times 10^{-8} \Rightarrow s^{3} = 0.8 \times 10^{-8} = 8 \times 10^{-9}$.

Taking the cube root, $s = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol/L}$.

The number of moles of $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ in $0.2 \text{ g}$ is $n = \dfrac{0.2 \text{ g}}{278 \text{ g/mol}} \approx 7.194 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$.

The volume $V$ required to dissolve this amount is $V = \dfrac{n}{s} = \dfrac{7.194 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}}{2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol/L}} = 0.3597 \text{ L}$.

Converting to milliliters, $V = 0.3597 \times 1000 \text{ ml} = 359.7 \text{ ml}$.

Answer: 359.7 ml

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A buffer solution has equal volumes of $0.1 \mathrm{~M} \mathrm{~NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ and $0.01 \mathrm{~M} \mathrm{~NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$. The $\mathrm{pK}_b$ of the base is 5. The $\mathrm{pH}$ is
questions.solution:
The buffer solution consists of a weak base $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ and its salt $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$. The concentration of the base $[\text{B}]$ is $0.1 \text{ M}$ and the concentration of the salt $[\text{BH}^+]$ is $0.01 \text{ M}$ after mixing equal volumes, as the dilution factor is the same for both.

Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for a basic buffer:

$\text{pOH} = \text{pK}_b + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]} \right)$

Given $\text{pK}_b = 5$, $[\text{salt}] = 0.01 \text{ M}$, and $[\text{base}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$:

$\text{pOH} = 5 + \log \left( \dfrac{0.01}{0.1} \right)$

$\text{pOH} = 5 + \log(10^{-1}) = 5 - 1 = 4$

The relationship between $\text{pH}$ and $\text{pOH}$ at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$ is $\text{pH} + \text{pOH} = 14$.

$\text{pH} = 14 - \text{pOH} = 14 - 4 = 10$

Answer: 10

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a $0.2 \mathrm{~M}$ aqueous solution, lactic acid is $6.9 \%$ dissociated. The value of dissociation constant is
questions.solution:
For a weak acid dissociation $HA \rightleftharpoons H^{+} + A^{-}$, the dissociation constant $K_a$ is given by the expression $K_a = \dfrac{c \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$.

Given concentration $c = 0.2 \text{ M}$ and degree of dissociation $\alpha = 6.9 \% = 0.069$.

Since $\alpha$ is small, we can approximate $1 - \alpha \approx 1$, so $K_a \approx c \alpha^2$.

Substituting the values: $K_a = 0.2 \times (0.069)^2$.

$K_a = 0.2 \times 0.004761 = 0.0009522$.

Expressing in scientific notation, $K_a = 9.522 \times 10^{-4} \approx 9.5 \times 10^{-4}$.

Answer: $9.5 \times 10^{-4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{pH}$ of $10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ solution of $\mathrm{KOH}$ is.
questions.solution:
KOH is a strong base, which dissociates completely in aqueous solution as follows:

$\mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{K}^{+} + \mathrm{OH}^{-}$

The concentration of hydroxide ions is equal to the concentration of the KOH solution:

$[\mathrm{OH}^{-}] = 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$

The pOH of the solution is calculated using the formula:

$\mathrm{pOH} = -\log[\mathrm{OH}^{-}] = -\log(10^{-3}) = 3$

Using the relation $\mathrm{pH} + \mathrm{pOH} = 14$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$:

$\mathrm{pH} = 14 - \mathrm{pOH} = 14 - 3 = 11$

Answer: 11
